H5574.name: Hassenuah
H5574.desc: Man who lived in Senaah@Ezr.2.35-Neh before the time of Exile and Return
H5574.brief: A leader from the tribe of Benjamin
H5574.short: Hassenuah (also known as Hassenaah) was a leader from the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

H5543A.name: Sallai
H5543A.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5543A.brief: Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the exile
H5543A.short: Sallai was a Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 11.

H5543D.name: Sallu
H5543D.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5543D.short: Sallu was a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem, as recorded in the genealogy of 1Chronicles 9.

H5543G.name: Sallu
H5543G.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5543G.brief: Benjamite who settled in Jerusalem after the exile
H5543G.short: Sallu was a Benjamite leader who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in Nehemiah 11.

H5543B.name: Sallu
H5543B.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5543B.brief: Priest who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel
H5543B.short: Sallu (or Sallai) was a priest who returned from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel and later signed the covenant under Nehemiah.

H5543C.name: Salu
H5543C.desc: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H5543C.brief: Father of Zimri, a Simeonite prince
H5543C.short: Salu was the father of Zimri, a Simeonite prince who was killed by Phinehas for his involvement with a Midianite woman.

H5562.name: Samgar
H5562.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5562.brief: Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem
H5562.short: Samgar was a Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem, as recorded in the book of Jeremiah.

H5571G.name: Sanballat
H5571G.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5571G.brief: Governor of Samaria, opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem
H5571G.short: Sanballat was the governor of Samaria who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

H5593.name: Saph
H5593.desc: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
H5593.brief: Philistine giant killed by Sibbechai the Hushathite
H5593.short: Saph (or Sippai) was a Philistine giant who was killed by Sibbechai the Hushathite during a battle with the Philistines.

H5540.name: Seled
H5540.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5540.brief: Son of Nadab, died without children
H5540.short: Seled, a son of Nadab, died without having any children.

H5565.name: Semachiah
H5565.desc: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5565.brief: Son of Shemaiah, gatekeeper of the temple
H5565.short: Semachiah, a son of Shemaiah, served as a gatekeeper in the temple during the time of David.

H5576.name: Sennacherib
H5576.desc: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5576.short: Sennacherib and Sargon were Assyrian kings who led military campaigns against Judah during the reigns of King Hezekiah and King Ahaz, respectively.

H5517.name: Siaha
H5517.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5517.brief: Ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.
H5517.short: Siaha (or Sia) was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

H5511.name: Sihon
H5511.desc: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
H5511.brief: Amorite king of Heshbon, defeated by the Israelites.
H5511.short: Sihon was the Amorite king of Heshbon who refused to let the Israelites pass through his land and was subsequently defeated by them.

H5513.name: Sinites
H5513.brief: Canaanite people group descended from Canaan.
H5513.short: The Sinites were a Canaanite people group descended from Canaan, the son of Ham.

H5516H.name: Sisera
H5516H.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
H5516H.brief: Ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.
H5516H.short: Sisera was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

H5516G.name: Sisera
H5516G.desc: Deborah's adversary living before Israel's Monarchy
H5516G.brief: Canaanite commander defeated by Deborah and Barak.
H5516G.short: Sisera was the commander of the Canaanite army who was defeated by the Israelites under the leadership of Deborah and Barak.

H5581.name: Sismai
H5581.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
H5581.short: Sismai was a descendant of Judah through Jerahmeel, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

H5525.name: Sukkiim
H5525.brief: African people who invaded Judah under Shishak
H5525.short: The Sukkiim were an African people who joined Shishak's invasion of Judah.

H5512A.name: Pelusium
H5512A.brief: An Egyptian city, also known as Sin
H5512A.short: Pelusium, also known as Sin, was an important Egyptian city mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy against Egypt.

H5555.name: Rock of Escape
H5555.brief: Place where Saul stopped pursuing David
H5555.short: The Rock of Escape was a place where Saul stopped pursuing David after being called away to fight the Philistines (<ref="1Sa. 23:28">1Sa. 23:28</ref>).
H5555.meaning: “the cliff of escapes” or “the cliff of divisions”

forms.meaning: “the cliff of escapes” or “the cliff of divisions”

H5548.name: Salecah
H5548.brief: City in Bashan, east of the Jordan River
H5548.short: Salecah was a city in the region of Bashan, east of the Jordan River, associated with the kingdoms of Og and Sihon (<ref="Deut. 3:10; Josh. 12:5; 13:11; 1Chr. 5:11">Deut. 3:10; Josh. 12:5; 13:11; 1Chr. 5:11</ref>).

H5578.name: Sansannah
H5578.brief: Town in the Negev region of Judah
H5578.short: Sansannah was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region (<ref="Josh. 15:31">Josh. 15:31</ref>).

H5527.name: Secacah
H5527.brief: Town in the wilderness of Judah
H5527.short: Secacah was a town located in the wilderness region of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:61">Josh. 15:61</ref>).

H5554.name: Sela
H5554.brief: Edomite stronghold captured by King Amaziah of Judah
H5554.short: Sela, also known as rock or Joktheel, was an Edomite stronghold captured by King Amaziah of Judah (<ref="2Ki. 14:7; 2Chr. 25:12; Isa. 16:1; 42:11; Judg. 1:36">2Ki. 14:7; 2Chr. 25:12; Isa. 16:1; 42:11; Judg. 1:36</ref>).

H5570G.name: Senaah
H5570G.brief: Town whose people returned from Babylonian exile
H5570G.short: Senaah was a town whose people are listed among those who returned to Judah from the Babylonian exile (<ref="Ezr. 2:35; Neh. 7:38">Ezr. 2:35; Neh. 7:38</ref>).

H5573.name: Seneh
H5573.short: Seneh was one of two rocky crags between which Jonathan and his armor-bearer passed to attack the Philistine garrison at Michmash (<ref="1Sam. 14:4">1Sam. 14:4</ref>).

H5538.name: Silla
H5538.brief: Place where King Joash was assassinated
H5538.short: Silla was the place where King Joash of Judah was assassinated by his servants (<ref="2Ki. 12:20">2Ki. 12:20</ref>).

H5512B.name: Sin
H5512B.brief: Wilderness area between Elim and Sinai
H5512B.short: Sin was a wilderness area between Elim and Sinai where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to the Promised Land (<ref="Exod. 16:1; 17:1; Num. 33:11-12">Exod. 16:1; 17:1; Num. 33:11-12</ref>).
H5512B.meaning: “thorn” or “clay” the tract of wilderness between Elim and Sinai

forms.meaning: “thorn” or “clay” the tract of wilderness between Elim and Sinai

H5514G.name: Sinai
H5514G.brief: Mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments
H5514G.short: Sinai, also called Mount Sinai, Horeb, or Mount Horeb, was the mountain where God gave Moses the Ten Commandments and other laws (<ref="Exod. 19-40; Lev. 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num. 3:1; 28:6; Deut. 33:2; Judg. 5:5; Ps. 68:8, 17; Neh. 9:13; Mal. 4:4; Act.7.30, 38; Gal. 4:24-25">Exod. 19-40; Lev. 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num. 3:1; 28:6; Deut. 33:2; Judg. 5:5; Ps. 68:8, 17; Neh. 9:13; Mal. 4:4; Act.7.30, 38; Gal. 4:24-25</ref>).

H5523H.name: Succoth
H5523H.brief: First Israelite campsite after leaving Egypt during Exodus
H5523H.short: Succoth, the first place the Israelites camped after leaving Egypt during the Exodus (<ref="Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5">Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5</ref>).

H5523G.name: Succoth
H5523G.brief: City in Canaan, location of Solomon's bronze works
H5523G.short: Succoth, a city in Canaan allocated to the tribe of Gad, later the site of Solomon's bronze works (<ref="Gen. 33:17; Josh. 13:27; 1Kgs. 7:46">Gen. 33:17; Josh. 13:27; 1Kgs. 7:46</ref>).

H5542.name: Selah
H5542.brief: A musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning
H5542.short: Selah is a term frequently used in the Psalms and Habakkuk, likely a musical or liturgical direction, though its precise meaning is uncertain (<ref="Psalm 3:2, 4, 8; Habakkuk 3:3, 9, 13">Psalm 3:2, 4, 8; Habakkuk 3:3, 9, 13</ref>).

H5522.name: Sikkuth
H5522.brief: A pagan deity worshipped by the Israelites
H5522.short: Sikkuth, possibly an Assyrian deity, was one of the pagan gods worshipped by the Israelites, for which they were condemned to exile (<ref="Amo.5.26">Amo.5.26</ref>).

H5510.name: Sivan
H5510.brief: The third month of the Jewish calendar
H5510.short: Sivan is the third month of the Jewish calendar, mentioned in <ref="Esther 8:9">Esther 8:9</ref> as the month in which Mordecai's decree was written and sent to the provinces.

H5524.name: Succoth-benoth
H5524.brief: A Babylonian deity worshipped by the Sepharvites
H5524.short: Succoth-benoth was a Babylonian deity worshipped by the Sepharvites, one of the peoples settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king (<ref="2Ki.17.30">2Ki.17.30</ref>).
